verses.1: Oh Ariel, Ariel! You are the place where David rested for years. The holidays will be celebrated here.
verses.2: And I was afflicted in Arieel. It became a place of suffering and pain for me. But it also became a place of comfort and joy for me.
verses.3: And I placed a burden upon you, and I made it difficult for you to move. I put obstacles in your way.
verses.4: And you will be brought low from the earth; your words will be heard no more. Your voice will become like sorrow that comes from the earth, and from the sky, your words will be silenced.
verses.5: And it would be like a tiny spot of dirt on your skin; or like a tiny speck of sand that’s scattered across your body. And suddenly, it would become something very small.
verses.6: With the power of Jehovah’s army, they will strike with violence and noise. There will be a loud noise, storm, and fire that burns everything.
verses.7: And it will be like a nightmare for the nations that live in Jerusalem. All those who dwell there, and all those who attack them.
verses.8: And it will be like when a person dreams of hunger, and then he sees food. His soul becomes exhausted and empty. And when he dreams of being cold, and then he feels cold, and his soul becomes empty and hollow. In the same way, all those nations that live on Mount Zion will be in that state.
verses.9: They became tired and exhausted. They were deceived and tricked. They lost their wages, and they received nothing in return.
verses.10: For Jehovah has sent a spirit upon you, so that your eyes will be dimmed, and your prophets and leaders will become blind.
verses.11: And you were given a vision of everything, just as it is written in the book that was given to the scribe. He said, “Read this.” But the scribe replied, “I cannot read it, for it is written on sealed tablets.”
verses.12: And the scribe gave him a book, but the scribe himself did not know how to read it. So he said, “Please read this for me.” But the scribe replied, “I don’t know how to read this book.”
verses.13: And Adonai said, “Because this people approach Me with their lips and their words, but their hearts are far from Me. Their fear of Me is due to the commands of men.”
verses.14: Therefore, I will bring about the destruction of this people, who are so foolish and stupid. The wisdom of their leaders will be destroyed, and their plans will fail.
verses.15: Oh, those who hide their plans from God! Their actions are known to Him. They said, “Who can see us? Who can know us?”
verses.16: If the creator is considered to be like coal, then it can be said that he did not create anything. He simply made something out of nothing. The creator himself didn’t understand what he was doing.
verses.17: It’s not yet too late; it can still be restored to its former state. The city of Jerusalem will be restored, and Jerusalem will become a forest again.
verses.18: And that day, the blind ones heard the words of the Book from the depths of darkness and from the hidden places. We shall see them.
verses.19: And the poor will be filled with joy in Jehovah’s love. And the people of Israel will rejoice in their holiness.
verses.20: For they were all wicked and evil; all their deeds were destroyed.
verses.21: The wicked of man are those who speak evil words and act deceitfully in the streets. They harm those who are good.
verses.22: Therefore, as Jehovah said to the house of Jacob, “I have saved Abraham. But now, Jacob will not be punished, nor will his face be covered.”
verses.23: For when his children saw his hands working in his own body, they honored my name. They also honored the holy name of Jacob and the God of Israel.
verses.24: And they shall know the ways of the spirit through understanding, and those who are wise will learn how to take things from others.
